bar.from: ROADMAP Sound 2.12: 1 dB in level or 0.1 in pan at the cue

master.what: the A mix (every switch off, the default blockout) normalized as scripts/sound.js does it, its own master giving a.wav; each option's set of mixes then goes through A's gain and one limiter curve from the loudest of the set at each sample (joint), or through one static gain low enough that none is limited (still, the characters' listener), so B over A is the option alone and nothing passes the ceiling

options.question: ROADMAP gate 2, question 3: the muffle on the hidden engine, done the PS1 way
options.definition: While the picture hides a placed cue's source (its rendered point through the frame's camera, a blocker between them, as Sound 1's onScreen check judges it), the voice is muffled, the PS1 way: volume, its volume drops by dropDb; swap, it crossfades to a copy of itself through a fixed lowpass, the pre-filtered sample a PS1 bank would hold (two voices in step while it is hidden). The hidden state is read per block and the muffle follows it over rampSec. It names every cue hidden on any frame it covers; the engine is the plan's case. Two hidden states: set (B, the plan's) and all (Sound 1's rule, for comparison)

dropDb.why: one tier of the level plan (SOUND-PLAN 1.3: a foreground sound sits at least 6 dB over the background, the midground 0 to 6 dB), so a hidden sound steps down by the gap between the two

lowpassHz.why: an octave under the darkest the air law reaches with distance (spatial.js SPATIAL.minAirHz, 1800 Hz), so the muffle reads as something in the way rather than far away; two 2-pole sections, as the placeholders build their bands (voices.js band)

rampSec.why: the backgrounds' crossfade at the place change (timbre.js TIMBRE.crossfadeSec): no click. A change of state is read at the next block (BLOCK samples, at most 5.3 ms after its frame), so the muffle has moved fully 50 to 55 ms after the frame that changes it

set.what: hidden by the set or by another body: a car's own body does not hide its own sounds (the plan's muffle, the engine behind building SE; the cabin and getting out stay hidden by the car, as sounds inside it)

all.what: Sound 1's onScreen rule (storyboard check 2): hidden by any blocker, a car's own body counted for its own sounds (the exhaust behind the rear bumper, the passenger door behind the car), for comparison

engine.what: the engine from its first hidden frame (building SE, shot 3) through the car coming into view

parts.what: the rise out of the quiet (hard.arrival.car.rise)
the intake behind building SE at full level
the intake in view; the set still hides the exhaust and the tyres for a few frames, Sound 1's rule the exhaust behind its own car

car.what: the 7 s where the muffle takes the most off the other hidden cues (10 onsets, all hidden by the car body)

placeholder.can: when the muffle acts (the frames the picture hides each source) and how much level it takes off each voice
placeholder.cannot: what a real muffle sounds like. The placeholders are narrow bands: the engine's buzz sits at 650 Hz, under the swap's 900 Hz cutoff, so the swap barely touches it, while a recorded engine has the high end a swap removes. The cabin's clicks (5.9 kHz) lose nearly everything. The swap's real effect on the engine is heard only at Sound 4

options.question: ROADMAP gate 2, question 3: a narrower pan for sync foley
options.definition: The pan of every foley cue of the kinds named (a family, or a family and its meta.kind) times widthRatio, from the camera as today; every other cue keeps its pan

widthRatio.why: halfway between the physical pan (1) and the centre (0): a midpoint to find out whether a narrower pan is audible at all, not a designed width. It puts the frame edge at 0.12 to 0.33 by lens instead of 0.24 to 0.66 (SOUND-PLAN 3.4)

kinds.why: the sync foley the task and the plan name: the steps, the scuffs and the hands' contacts (the forearms coming to rest on the parapet, the hands cupping the lighter). Cloth on the walks, turns and shifts is not a contact and keeps its pan

pan.what: the 7 s where the sync foley's pan moves the most (15 onsets moving by 0.1 or more)

placeholder.can: the pan itself: the spatializer pans by level alone, so a band-limited step moves exactly as a real one would
placeholder.cannot: how wide the stereo image feels against real backgrounds and real steps, whose high end localizes better than a 1.25 kHz band; and whether the wide image distracts on a phone (mono there either way)

options.question: ROADMAP gate 2, question 3: the second listener model, level from the characters and pan from the camera
options.definition: The level of every placed voice by its own distance law from the characters' point: the mean of the cloth points (each poser's root plus 1.2 m, DESIGN.CLOTH.up) of the people out of the car, whether or not the camera sees them (the poser's presence), one person while only one is out, the camera's level before anyone is (until 30.9 s, just before A's first frame out of the car). The pan, the air lowpass and the dark behind the camera stay the camera's. A cue's level is its loudest 100 ms (the level plan's measure)

listener.why: the storyboard's own characters model (scripts/sound-report.js hear), so the render can be checked against what Sound 1 predicted at every cut

listener.what: the 7 s where the levels move the most (19 onsets whose loudest 100 ms moves by 1 dB or more)

placeholder.can: every level change the model makes, cue by cue and at the moment the people appear
placeholder.cannot: the balance those levels make with real sounds (SOUND-PLAN 4.4: balance is reported at Sound 2, not judged)

options.question: ROADMAP gate 2, question 2: the style-frame scene to design first in Sound 4
options.definition: Runs of whole shots, up to 32 s (the default's 24 s and a third: a scene the director hears before the rest), chosen by rule from the cues; each with its facts from the cues and the storyboard's density and voices checks

scenes.name: default
scenes.why: ROADMAP Sound gate 2: every category, the densest moment and the hush after the engine dies (SOUND-PLAN 3.17)

scenes.name: most families, shortest
scenes.why: the shortest run of whole shots up to 32 s with the most families

scenes.name: both places
scenes.why: the shortest run up to 32 s with the most families that reaches the street and the bridge

scenes.name: what the default leaves out
scenes.why: the shortest run up to 32 s holding every family the default has none of (water, lighter, drag, breath)

placeholder.can: which cues, families, places and quiet each scene holds
placeholder.cannot: which scene sets the style best: that is heard, at Sound 4
